sourceIdentity.scopeCaveat: The fingerprints use different file-selection commands and are not expected to match. The 9e381 scope binds the preceding dependency/import A/B audit; the 0af9 scope binds the final current Xcode Release build and latest canonical export.
sourceIdentity.artifactIdentityCaveat: Source fingerprints identify the audited source scopes; artifact hashes identify only their concrete build products. Generated Hermes bytecode is not a deterministic source fingerprint: a repeated Expo export from unchanged source was observed to differ by one byte and SHA because an Expo temporary path was embedded. The canonical Expo export and Xcode's embedded bundle are separate build invocations, so byte equality between them is not implied.

finalSignedXcodeRelease.warningCapture: The exact warning-line count is unavailable because direct build-tool output was truncated. Observed warnings were in dependency or generated bundle paths; no application-source error was reported.

canonicalExpoExport.deliveryModel: One native Hermes bytecode bundle. Expo Router defers route evaluation, but this build does not create native import() chunks.

cuaAcceptance.driver: Computer Use through the Simulator accessibility tree; simctl openurl was used only for controlled route setup
cuaAcceptance.timingAndIndexCaveat: Simulator CUA element indices and action delivery occasionally lagged or changed after navigation. The replay used separate state/action calls, repeated stable-state captures, screenshots or coordinates, and controlled deep links. CUA route brackets include tool transport, accessibility serialization, delayed action delivery, and settling; they are not app-only timings or frame-pacing measurements. The wide-thread second-sheet tap and group-list scrolling were specifically confounded by this tooling behavior, so cursor/reachability claims also rely on API, source, and automated-test evidence.

remainingPerformanceRisksFromCodeAudit: Broad global context subscriptions can fan out renders across otherwise unrelated mobile surfaces.
Sidebar derivation scans and indexes a broad snapshot and still scales with the full roster.
Global message merging performs an O(N log N) sort and some consumers perform another sort or trim.
The active channel can retain every explicitly loaded history page in JavaScript memory; mounted rows are bounded, backing state is not.
Outgoing snapshot serialization can re-sort the full message collection.
Snapshot cursor changes can invalidate search cache entries and cause abort/refetch churn.
The 64-entry mobile search LRU is count-bounded rather than byte-bounded; unusually large result URLs could consume substantial memory.
Fixture fallback constructs all categories eagerly.
The composer statically imports picker surfaces, and the native build is a single Hermes bundle rather than route chunks.
